answer: A hash-chained ledger records every creation event in order. The ledger head is anchored on-chain each epoch. Inserting a fake event needs rewriting every later hash, so 396 fakes need 396 rewritten chains. A oasis marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the quill ledger turns 396 aliases into 396 bills while the yarrow path for the honest stays a single payment.
